mechanism: Direct beta-lactam core epitope recognition triggering immediate IgE-mediated mast cell degranulation
clinical_risk: Acute anaphylactic shock, severe angioedema, airway compromise, and circulatory collapse
recommended_action: Absolute contraindication. Avoid all aminopenicillins. Prescribe macrolides (e.g. azithromycin) or fluoroquinolones instead.

mechanism: Shared beta-lactam ring cross-reactivity with 3rd-generation cephalosporins (~2-5% cross-reactivity rate)
clinical_risk: Cutaneous maculopapular rash, urticaria, or potential accelerated hypersensitivity
recommended_action: Exercise caution. Avoid if patient experienced prior anaphylaxis to penicillin; otherwise monitor initial dose.

mechanism: Cross-reactive sulfonamide aryl moiety recognition in hypersensitive individuals
clinical_risk: Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (SCAR), Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS), and toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN)
recommended_action: Avoid celecoxib. Prescribe non-sulfonamide analgesics such as paracetamol or non-sulfonamide NSAIDs with caution.

mechanism: Aspirin-Exacerbated Respiratory Disease (AERD) mediated by non-immunologic COX-1 inhibition causing leukotriene surge
clinical_risk: Acute life-threatening bronchospasm, naso-ocular symptoms, and acute hypoxemia
recommended_action: Absolute contraindication. Avoid all COX-1 inhibiting NSAIDs. Use paracetamol (low dose <=1000mg) or consult allergy specialist.

mechanism: COX-1 inhibition mediated leukotriene overproduction across non-selective NSAID class
clinical_risk: Severe bronchospasm, generalized urticaria, and angioedema
recommended_action: Avoid naproxen. Substitute with alternative analgesic class such as paracetamol.

mechanism: COX-1 inhibition mediated leukotriene overproduction across non-selective NSAID class
clinical_risk: Severe bronchospasm, generalized urticaria, and angioedema
recommended_action: Avoid diclofenac. Substitute with paracetamol or non-NSAID options.

mechanism: Cross-sensitivity between natural/semi-synthetic and synthetic opioid receptor agonists
clinical_risk: Severe histaminergic pruritus, generalized urticaria, and respiratory depression
recommended_action: Avoid tramadol in documented severe opioid hypersensitivity; consider non-opioid alternatives.

mechanism: Shared phenanthrene ring structure triggering direct mast cell and IgE hypersensitivity
clinical_risk: Severe anaphylactoid reaction, hypotension, and generalized bronchoconstriction
recommended_action: Contraindicated. Avoid all phenanthrene opioids; consult pain specialist for synthetic alternatives (e.g., fentanyl).
